summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, chronic constipation, and polysubstance use was admitted for left-sided abdominal pain. Evaluation revealed no evidence of pyelonephritis or DVT; pain was attributed to constipation and recent cocaine use. She remained afebrile with stable labs, and her symptoms improved with supportive care, including pain management and bowel regimen. Elevated liver enzymes were noted, likely due to NASH and drug use. Medications were adjusted: amitriptyline and iron were discontinued, and Maalox was added for abdominal discomfort. She was discharged home with instructions to continue bowel regimen, monitor for pain recurrence, and follow up for INR and liver function testing.
